newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, Iran, Turkmens sign Caspian mineral deal.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Iran, Turkmens sign Caspian mineral deal.

text.p: Foreign ministers from Russia, Iran and Turkmenistan have signed a memorandum agreeing to cooperate in developing mineral resources around the Caspian Sea, Russian news agencies said on Wednesday.

"We intend to create a joint company to explore and exploit hydrocarbon materials in the coastal zones of the three states," Itar-Tass quoted Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov as saying after the signing in the Turkmen capital Ashgabat on Tuesday.
Interfax quoted him as saying the agreement was open to other Caspian states and international investors. The founding documents could be signed no later than December, he added.
Primakov told a news conference Moscow was ready to recognise the oilfields of neighbouring states outside a 45-mile (72 km) coastal zone in the Caspian.
Russia had previously argued that the sea was a lake whose resources should be developed and shared equally by all the littoral states -- Russia, Iran, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan.

Primakov and the foreign ministers of Iran, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan met to thrash out the legal status of the Caspian Sea which was divided up between the Soviet Union and Iran first in 1921 and again in 1940.
Since the break up of the Soviet Union, the Caspian has become the subject of an intense diplomatic and legal battle over the area's immense reserves of oil and gas.

The focus of the present battle rages over whether the Caspian is a sea or a lake. Academics argue the sea is actually a salt-water lake but the control of billions of dollars worth of black gold ride on the apparently arcane question.

The Caspian ranks eighth in the world in terms of discovered oil reserves. Reserves in Kazakhstan's continental shelf of the Caspian alone are 10 billion tonnes. The sea has not been fully studied and may hold much more.
No agreement was reached at the meeting on the Caspian Sea's status but a Turkmen Foreign Ministry spokesman said the five countries would meet again to discuss the issue in Kazakhstan in December.
